newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee forex intervention continues-RBI chief.
newsitem.headline: India rupee forex intervention continues-RBI chief.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will continue to intervene to stop the rupee from strengthening but a resulting boost to monetary growth was a constraint, the central bank chief said in a newspaper interview on Wednesday.

"We have to look at the monetary impact of the intervention and also look at the real effective exchange rate and try to achieve some balance," the RBI governor C. Rangarajan told the Financial Express daily.
He said the central bank was intervening in the currency market in response to a question whether the RBI would help exporters by encouraging a gradual depreciation in the rupee.
"I think this is one action we are taking," he said.
Rangarajan also said a medium term target for the central bank was to reduce banks' cash reserve ratio (CRR) further below the current 10 percent.
"We will have to see what is warranted in the present circumstances," he said. "On the removal of CRR on interbank borrowings, these are all matters under consideration," he said.

The central bank chief said the dollar has gained substantially in the last 15 months against other major international currencies, while the rupee/dollar rate has been been very stable for the last nine months.
The rupee traded at 35.84 to the dollar on Wednesday.
"Therefore, we certainly look at the real, effective exchange rate," he said.
The trade-weighted real effective exchange rate index stood at 63.05 in September 1996, according to lates RBI data, compared to 63.58 in September 1995.
"We do not have a target for the level of foreign exchange reserves," he said. Currency reserves stood at 20.09 on March 6.
"Moreover, the intervention will be limited by the impact it (such intervention) has on money supply," Rangarajan said.
He said RBI intervention should not lead to any overshoot of a targetted 16 percent growth in M3 in 1997/98 (April-March).
